title: Medieval Rimworld + Kenshi made with Fable 5.2
author: 2nd_breakfastt
selftext:
Hey all, I’m 50 builds into Valdmark, a top-down medieval sandbox inspired by games like Kenshi and RimWorld.

My vision is that you start as nobody and can make a living however you want. Trading, blacksmithing, farming, exploring, fighting, or eventually building your own settlement.

I’m building it in Godot with GDScript and using Fable 5.2 to help with coding and development. It’s been a lot of testing, breaking things, fixing them, building tools to help with development, research and lots of time figuring out what actually makes the game fun.

It’s at the point now where I’m focusing on the juice of the game and polishing up pretty much everything: cleaner buildings, cleaner animations, additional biomes etc.

One thing I’m trying to nail down is making professions enjoyable enough that you could spend a whole playthrough as a blacksmith or merchant without feeling like you’re missing the real game.  
Here’s the current gameplay trailer.  
Curious what other devs think of the scope and gameplay loop. Is there anything you’d focus on first?

comments.author: Offbeat_voyage
comments.body: First off i love the music and admire your ambition to dream big, how would you say your game is different from both Kenshi and rimworld? Those are big shoes to fill two both overwhelmingly postive games. I am really excited to see what you will make and added it to my saved list

replies.author: 2nd_breakfastt
replies.body:
Hey thanks means a lot. I think the biggest difference I’m aiming for is making ordinary medieval life just as rewarding as combat or building an empire. I want someone to be able to spend an entire playthrough as a blacksmith, merchant, or farmer if they wanted and still have meaningful progression and gameplay

Currently I’m putting a lot of focus on professions, production chains, town economies, and a world that keeps moving without you. Definitely taking inspiration from both games, but trying to build something where making a living can be the whole adventure.

I’m planning to have a demo released soon, would love to hear more of your feedback after giving it a play!

replies.author: c00ld0c26
replies.body: One thing I always kind of missed in skill progressions is how the world reacts. Like if I have a an extremely skilled blacksmith and he has been selling his work for a while, I'd expect him to develop a reputation and become recognizeable as more of his work ends up in the world. Maybe you can even find certain people using your merchandise as you travel. Just an idea for the progression aspect that I feel like a lot of games miss.

replies.author: 2nd_breakfastt
replies.body: Hey agreed and that’s actually one of the exact elements I’m looking to add to the game. You build up a reputation in your surrounding area and word gets around that you or one of your characters is a masters blacksmith (any profession, and once they reach that level) and youre able to craft better items, begin to see more expensive contracts come in, mercenaries in the area learn you sell the best weapons, a lord may hire you to arm his soldiers etc. I like the touch of seeing you’re crafted items out and about being used in the world, ill add thst to the notes thanks!

comments.author: 2nd_breakfastt
comments.body:
Some of the main features I’m working on:

**Infinite procedural world** — Every playthrough generates a different world with no map boundaries, so there’s always somewhere new to explore.

**8 starting origins** — Start as a wanderer, merchant, survivor, group of settlers, mercenary company, etc.

**Skill progression** — 16 skills that improve through use, with mastery ranks and specializations.

**Professions & crafting** — Blacksmithing, farming, carpentry, trading, and production chains.

**Dynamic economy** — Different town markets, supply and demand, trading caravans, and contracts.

**Settlement building** — Start with a camp and work toward a fully functioning fortified settlement.

**Living world** — Roaming bandits, travelers, changing seasons, survival needs, and random encounters.

The big goal is that there’s no required path. You can spend your whole playthrough mastering a trade, exploring, or building something of your own.

comments.author: Arcayon
comments.body: oh hey we are making the same game kinda

replies.author: 2nd_breakfastt
replies.body: Hell yeah. Big scope, lots of fun play testing tho

comments.author: OneMoreFightGame
comments.body: Yo this looks sick! Those two games are among my favorite games ever. Are you going to do open playtests at some point?

replies.author: 2nd_breakfastt
replies.body:
Appreciate it! I’ve sunk so many hours into both of those games haha. My goal is to have a demo out this weekend

Right now I’m working on overhauling the buildings with a modular system.. so structures feel more unique and can visually change depending on their upgrades and functions

also adding a cave system for exploration and resource gathering, and bringing the production lines to life with actual animations, so you can watch workers go through the different steps of crafting instead of resources just magically turning into finished products

Once I get those systems polished up, I think I’ll be pretty happy with where the game is for a first demo!

Itch page will be up soon, stay tuned! Here’s a sneak peak of the cave system 

https://i.redd.it/ftbtxa0xcd2i1.jpeg

comments.author: crackedpotstudio
comments.body:
I really love to see all these mega ''scopecreep'' projects popping up and would love to follow this project.

I'm currently trying something similar to spend my last tokens before the weekly reset, zoomed out it's a grand strategy (think of hoi4 in modern times) but you can actually zoom all the way in to street level and play individual battles as an RTS. Totally ridiculously and over the top to actually generate the whole world in an RTS but we'll see how far I get.
